Hi Olivia — great to hear the team is aligned to run a pilot. I pulled together three pragmatic options focused on hosted API usage and an onramp credit structure that ties to commit. Summary attached (20270420_redwood_onramp_pricing_v2.xlsx) and a short MA plan in the docx. TL;DR below: 

Option A — Conversion-starter pilot (no upfront commit):
- 100k USD in credits for 8-week pilot (covering metadata + heavy logging)
- Post-pilot: pay-as-you-go rates, no committed discount
- Use case: validation only, low friction to start

Option B — 3-month committed onramp (recommended for cost predictability):
- 150k USD credit applied over first 90 days against usage
- Commit: 9M tokens/month (avg) for 3 months; per-token discount 8% off list for generation tokens, 6% for embeddings
- If actual usage exceeds commit by >20% we bill incremental at the committed rate; unused commit converts to account credit during first renewal period

Option C — Launch+scale (preferred if you plan to ship to customers quickly):
- 300k USD in credits across a 3-month ramp, split into pilot and launch pools
- Commit: 12M tokens/month for 6 months, with stepped discounts: 12% for months 1–3, 15% for months 4–6
- Includes 1 dedicated onboarding sync, priority support, and one performance tuning pass

Key notes:
- Credits are one-time, non-refundable, applied against billed usage; pilot credits require a signed MA/SA with conversion language (simple template attached).
- We can add an SLA uplift for Dedicated later but pilot is on Hosted API.
- SOC 2 and security artifacts available on request — we can provide an evidence bundle for procurement.

Next steps I suggest: 1) pick A/B/C, 2) we issue a short MA + SOW, 3) procurement/finance executes and we schedule onboarding.

I copied Marissa (rev ops) to help with contract and Karthik to assist on pricing/PO logic.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call later today.

Sergio Alvarez

Sergio / Marissa —

Thanks for the clear options. A few procurement questions before we move legal: 

1) We prefer credits that are applied only to hosted consumption invoices (not professional services). Can you confirm the credit scoping?
2) For Option B: can you reduce the minimum commit to 6M tokens/month for a 3-month term and keep the 8% discount? Our initial burst is uncertain — we'd rather hedge upward.
3) If we take Option C but don't hit the month 4–6 ramp, is there a true-up mechanism or can unused credits be retained for 30 days post-term?

Also, SOC 2 Type II report would be required for our security review. If you can include a checklist of security artifacts we can expedite legal.

Regards,
Daniel Ruiz
Director, Cloud Integrations — Enterpratek

Subject: Re: Exploring pilot credits and commit options

Daniel — thanks for the questions, good clarifying points. Answers inline: 

1) Credit scoping: credits apply only to hosted API billed usage (generation + embeddings + reranking). They do NOT apply to professional services (onboarding, SLO engineering) or one-off third-party pass-throughs. We'll call this out in the MA (see attached SOW template).

2) Commit floor flexibility: we can support 6M tokens/month for a 3-month committed onramp and preserve the 8% discount. The smaller commit moves some of the upfront credit into a refundable pool that converts to account credit if you don't convert to a longer term — details in MA.

3) True-up / unused credits: for Option C we can allow unused credits to be retained for 30 days post-term and then expire, or convert to a 60-day retention for a nominal admin fee. Alternatively, we can stagger the credits to favor months 1–2 for pilot validation and month 3 reserved for discovery-to-launch conversion. We'll put the exact language in the MA appendix.

Security artifacts: we will provide SOC 2 Type II, penetration test summary, and a redacted architecture diagram. I'll ask our security team to drop the evidence bundle into the Drive link I shared.

Proposed next step: I updated the pricing workbook with a 6M tokens/month line and an explicit credit scoping section. If you are comfortable, Marissa and I can draft the MA + SOW and route to your procurement for signature; we can keep timelines to under 7 business days from acceptance.

Would you be available for a 30-min call tomorrow to finalize which option?

Thanks,
Sergio
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
